note: Franky's notebook. Written by the duck itself (the model's weights never change). tries = attempts the note was shown in, wins = how many of those succeeded.

knowledge.text: Walking forward 0.2 m (Step 20) was refused because it would run into the box rim.
Moving and turning does not guarantee the target objects will be visible in subsequent pictures (Steps 17, 19, 22).
Walking stops if an object is detected right at the feet (Step 11).
The vision model may fail to find objects, even if they were previously located (Step 14).
Walking commands sometimes result in unexpected turns (e.g., moving forward 0.30 m resulted in a 7 degree left turn).
The beak fails to pick up the banana even when the beak sense indicates it is within the 0.10 m pickup range.

skills.text: To pick up the banana, ensure the distance is less than 0.10 m from the beak tip.
When searching for objects after moving, look carefully to confirm visibility before assuming they are gone.
If approaching an object, check if walking stops early due to proximity.
When searching for objects, assume they might be temporarily invisible after movement.
Before attempting pickup, confirm the target object is aligned with the direction of approach.
After any movement, always re-scan the area to confirm the visibility of all target objects.
